text.en: Real-time forecasting, anomaly detection, and optimization, powered by IBM time-series models with more than 50 million downloads. Now available natively on Confluent, in the cloud and on premises, running on CPUs.
text.th: Real-time forecasting, anomaly detection, and optimization, powered by IBM time-series models with more than 50 million downloads. Now available natively on Confluent, in the cloud and on premises, running on CPUs.

text.en: Every business generates a continuous record of change: a machine reading, a payment, a sale, an order, or a change in inventory. These observations form time series, and they carry signals that can help teams anticipate what happens next.
text.th: Every business generates a continuous record of change: a machine reading, a payment, a sale, an order, or a change in inventory. These observations form time series, and they carry signals that can help teams anticipate what happens next.

text.en: The challenge is turning those signals into decisions while they still matter. A forecast delivered after a production run, a stockout, or a payment authorization may be accurate, but too late to influence the outcome.
text.th: The challenge is turning those signals into decisions while they still matter. A forecast delivered after a production run, a stockout, or a payment authorization may be accurate, but too late to influence the outcome.

text.en: IBM and Confluent are bringing time-series foundation models closer to the data as it flows. With Apache Flink, teams can apply forecasting , anomaly detection and semantic intelligence to streaming data using SQL, making model outputs available to the applications and people responsible for the next action.
text.th: IBM and Confluent are bringing time-series foundation models closer to the data as it flows. With Apache Flink, teams can apply forecasting , anomaly detection and semantic intelligence to streaming data using SQL, making model outputs available to the applications and people responsible for the next action.

text.en: Foundation models have changed how organizations work with text, images, and documents. Time-series foundation models extend a similar idea to numerical data by learning general patterns from diverse historical data and then applying that knowledge to new series and tasks. The models can provide a starting point without requiring teams to train a separate model for every series. Depending on the task and deployment, teams can also fine-tune a model or combine its outputs with other data and business logic.

text.en: Now the time series foundation models run natively inside Confluent as built-in functions in the cloud and on premises. In Confluent Cloud they are fully managed, with nothing to deploy (documentation). On premises, the models can run within your own infrastructure using Confluent Platform for Apache Flink.(documentation). The models run on CPUs, without requiring GPUs.

text.en: The models can support a range of mission-critical use cases, from helping keep production lines in spec and detecting unusual store activity to improving product-level planning. They can also provide signals to assess card payments and forecast trading volume to help place large orders. These building blocks can be applied across manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines, bringing insights closer to where decisions are made.

text.en: Streamhouse: real-time data and intelligence for agentic era
text.th: Streamhouse: real-time data and intelligence for agentic era

text.en: Businesses operate continuously. Orders are updated, payments arrive, shipments are delayed, and inventory changes throughout the day. Yet the information behind these events often sits across systems that update at different times or rely on periodic batch processes. When applications and AI agents act on outdated or inconsistent information, they risk making decisions that no longer reflect what is happening.
text.th: Businesses operate continuously. Orders are updated, payments arrive, shipments are delayed, and inventory changes throughout the day. Yet the information behind these events often sits across systems that update at different times or rely on periodic batch processes. When applications and AI agents act on outdated or inconsistent information, they risk making decisions that no longer reflect what is happening.

text.en: A Streamhouse addresses this by continuously capturing, processing, governing, and serving current business context. Confluent’s Data Streaming Platform brings together five capabilities—connect, stream, process, govern, and query—to make that context available to applications, analytics, and agents. Apache Flink transforms and enriches data as it flows, while Lightning Tables provide low-latency access to the current state.
text.th: A Streamhouse addresses this by continuously capturing, processing, governing, and serving current business context. text.en: Figure 2. The Streamhouse on Confluent: from existing data sources to current business context that agents, applications, analytics and lakehouses use anywhere.

text.en: Time-series models add predictive power to this architecture. Flink can prepare the data, invoke forecasting and anomaly detection, and make the results available alongside the events that produced them. Other models—including large language models, statistical models, and specialized machine learning systems—can contribute where appropriate.

text.en: This approach can help teams in four ways:
text.th: This approach can help teams in four ways:

text.en: -Scale model development. A pretrained model can provide a common starting point across many time series, reducing the need to develop and maintain a separate model for each one.
text.th: -Scale model development. A pretrained model can provide a common starting point across many time series, reducing the need to develop and maintain a separate model for each one.

text.en: -Refresh predictions as data changes. Forecasts can incorporate recent observations as part of a streaming workflow, subject to the model’s requirements and the pipeline’s configuration.
text.th: -Refresh predictions as data changes. Forecasts can incorporate recent observations as part of a streaming workflow, subject to the model’s requirements and the pipeline’s configuration.

text.en: -Put signals closer to decisions. Forecasts and anomalies can be routed to operational applications sooner, where teams can combine them with business context, rules, and human judgment.
text.th: -Put signals closer to decisions. Forecasts and anomalies can be routed to operational applications sooner, where teams can combine them with business context, rules, and human judgment.

text.en: -Run compact models on CPUs. The models are small enough to run on standard CPUs alongside the streaming pipeline, in the cloud or on premises, which can reduce the need for dedicated GPU infrastructure and simplify deployment.

text.en: Use Case 1 | Production optimization: every tub in spec
text.th: Use Case 1 | Production optimization: every tub in spec

text.en: An ice cream line’s quality depends on overrun—the amount of air whipped into the mix. Today, the process engineer and operator rely on QA lab measurements taken after the tubs are filled. If a new cream lot or a warm, humid day changes the process, hours of production may already need rework by the time the team sees the result.
text.th: An ice cream line’s quality depends on overrun—the amount of air whipped into the mix. Today, the process engineer and operator rely on QA lab measurements taken after the tubs are filled. If a new cream lot or a warm, humid day changes the process, hours of production may already need rework by the time the team sees the result.

text.en: To get ahead of the problem, a pretrained TTM model reads SCADA telemetry and QA measurements every 10 minutes. It forecasts the share of tubs expected to be in spec four hours ahead, along with a likely range.
text.th: To get ahead of the problem, a pretrained TTM model reads SCADA telemetry and QA measurements every 10 minutes. It forecasts the share of tubs expected to be in spec four hours ahead, along with a likely range.

text.en: When the forecast falls below the plant’s target, an optimization process evaluates combinations of freezer draw temperature and airflow. Because the model takes these control variables as inputs, it can score each option before anything changes on the line. The operator approves the recommended setpoints, while routine adjustments can be automated within predefined guardrails.
text.th: When the forecast falls below the plant’s target, an optimization process evaluates combinations of freezer draw temperature and airflow. Because the model takes these control variables as inputs, it can score each option before anything changes on the line. The operator approves the recommended setpoints, while routine adjustments can be automated within predefined guardrails.

text.en: The outcome is a more proactive process: less rework, lower energy use per tonne, and more consistent quality. The same approach can be applied to ovens, dryers, kilns, and mills.
text.th: The outcome is a more proactive process: less rework, lower energy use per tonne, and more consistent quality. The same approach can be applied to ovens, dryers, kilns, and mills.

text.en: Use Case 2 | Anomaly detection: from a flag to the right action
text.th: Use Case 2 | Anomaly detection: from a flag to the right action

text.en: A store operations team monitors sales for thousands of products across hundreds of stores. Fixed thresholds often flag predictable weekend peaks while missing quieter changes, such as a product selling less than expected. As alerts accumulate, it becomes harder for the team to know where to focus.
text.th: A store operations team monitors sales for thousands of products across hundreds of stores. Fixed thresholds often flag predictable weekend peaks while missing quieter changes, such as a product selling less than expected. As alerts accumulate, it becomes harder for the team to know where to focus.

text.en: AI_DETECT_ANOMALIES gives each sales series an expected range based on its recent history. Each new reading is compared with that range at a confidence level the team chooses, without training a separate model for every product and store.
text.th: AI_DETECT_ANOMALIES gives each sales series an expected range based on its recent history. Each new reading is compared with that range at a confidence level the team chooses, without training a separate model for every product and store.

text.en: When sales fall outside the expected range, the signal can be combined with inventory and store data to help identify a likely cause and recommend a next step—for example, checking the shelf or replenishing stock. The same approach can be applied to machine sensors, API telemetry, meter readings, and payment volumes.

text.en: Use Case 3 | Supply chain planning: every SKU, every store, every hour
text.th: Use Case 3 | Supply chain planning: every SKU, every store, every hour

text.en: A category planner and a replenishment team need to keep products available across every store without carrying excess inventory. But forecasts may be refreshed only once a week, often focusing on top-selling products, while the long tail is managed with simpler rules. When sales patterns change between planning cycles, one store can run out while another has too much stock.
text.th: A category planner and a replenishment team need to keep products available across every store without carrying excess inventory. But forecasts may be refreshed only once a week, often focusing on top-selling products, while the long tail is managed with simpler rules. When sales patterns change between planning cycles, one store can run out while another has too much stock.

text.en: With AI_FORECAST, a pretrained model can forecast demand across products and stores. In this example, it produces a 28-day forecast with a P10–P90 range, refreshed as new sales data arrives. The planning application combines the forecast with inventory, lead time, and the planner’s chosen service level to calculate a reorder point.
text.th: With AI_FORECAST, a pretrained model can forecast demand across products and stores. In this example, it produces a 28-day forecast with a P10–P90 range, refreshed as new sales data arrives. The planning application combines the forecast with inventory, lead time, and the planner’s chosen service level to calculate a reorder point.

text.en: When stock is projected to fall below that point, an agent can draft a purchase order for review. The same approach can support planning for spare parts, staffing, ATM cash, and energy demand.
text.th: When stock is projected to fall below that point, an agent can draft a purchase order for review. The same approach can support planning for spare parts, staffing, ATM cash, and energy demand.

text.en: Use Case 4 | Fraud and security: every card has its own normal
text.th: Use Case 4 | Fraud and security: every card has its own normal

text.en: Fraud teams already rely on sophisticated rules and models to evaluate transactions. One continuing challenge is that a threshold applied across many cardholders may not reflect how each person normally spends.
text.th: Fraud teams already rely on sophisticated rules and models to evaluate transactions. One continuing challenge is that a threshold applied across many cardholders may not reflect how each person normally spends.

text.en: A time-series signal can add that individual context. In this example, each payment is compared with an expected spending range based on the card’s recent history. A transaction outside that range is passed to the bank’s existing fraud systems as an additional input, alongside other signals and business rules.
text.th: A time-series signal can add that individual context. In this example, each payment is compared with an expected spending range based on the card’s recent history. A transaction outside that range is passed to the bank’s existing fraud systems as an additional input, alongside other signals and business rules.

text.en: The bank can then decide whether to approve the payment, request additional authentication, or investigate further. The decision and the signals behind it can be retained for review.

text.en: Use Case 5 | Trading: pace the order with the tape
text.th: Use Case 5 | Trading: pace the order with the tape

text.en: An execution desk needs to divide a large order into smaller trades while managing its effect on the market. Historical volume curves offer a starting point, but today’s trading activity may look very different from the average.
text.th: An execution desk needs to divide a large order into smaller trades while managing its effect on the market. Historical volume curves offer a starting point, but today’s trading activity may look very different from the average.

text.en: On each one-minute bar, PatchTST-FM forecasts trading volume for the next 30 minutes, with a P10–P90 range. The execution algorithm uses that forecast to pace the order within the participation limit set by the desk.
text.th: On each one-minute bar, PatchTST-FM forecasts trading volume for the next 30 minutes, with a P10–P90 range. The execution algorithm uses that forecast to pace the order within the participation limit set by the desk.

text.en: If a news event changes market activity, the algorithm can pause and replan. If trading is quieter than expected, it can reduce the size of each slice and signal that the order may take longer to complete. Each forecast and the resulting execution decisions can be retained in the audit trail.

text.en: Use Case 6 | Semantic search: find every signal that looks like this
text.th: Use Case 6 | Semantic search: find every signal that looks like this

text.en: A reliability engineer investigating an unusual sensor pattern may want to know whether similar behavior appeared elsewhere in the plant.
text.th: A reliability engineer investigating an unusual sensor pattern may want to know whether similar behavior appeared elsewhere in the plant.

text.en: TSPulse can produce representations of time-series windows that support similarity search. In a separately built application, those representations could be indexed and used to retrieve historical patterns across equipment. An engineer could search for shapes such as a spike and recovery, a gradual rise, or a step change, then inspect the associated maintenance records and operating conditions.

In a separately built application, those representations could be indexed and used to retrieve historical patterns across equipment. An engineer could search for shapes such as a spike and recovery, a gradual rise, or a step change, then inspect the associated maintenance records and operating conditions.

text.en: This application requires an embedding pipeline, an index, and access to the relevant context. Similarity can help narrow an investigation; it does not establish a root cause by itself.

text.en: Industrial AI: from sensor to setpoint. The plant manager wants every batch in spec and no line stopped by a surprise. SCADA, QA lab and energy meter streams are forecast as they arrive. Production optimization moves the setpoints when quality starts to drift, anomaly detection flags the reading no rule was written for, and semantic search finds every pump that showed the same pattern before a failure. Setpoints, work orders and alerts reach the floor inside the cycle, not at the next shift report.

text.en: Retail: a store and its supply chain. The store manager wants a full shelf on Saturday without overstock on Monday. Sales, weather and promotion streams are forecast for every product in every store. Supply chain planning sets the order, anomaly detection catches the empty shelf or the missed delivery, and fraud and security holds the suspicious card. Orders, store tasks and holds go out before the shelf runs empty.

text.en: Banking: payments and the trading desk. The fraud lead wants to stop card testing without blocking good customers, and the trader wants a large order done without moving the price. Every card and every symbol is scored against its own expected pattern, event by event. Fraud and security holds the odd swipe before authorization, anomaly detection spots the unusual flow, and trading paces each order with the forecast volume.
